$comment: ACKNOWLEDGED findings for inert-valuesobject-keys.ts.
WHAT AN ENTRY IS. Not a suppression -- a dated, keyed, reasoned record that a `valuesObject` key
governs NOTHING and is not being repaired in the change that discovered it. Every acknowledged
finding is still printed by the report and still costs exactly what it costs; what the entry buys
is a non-red gate, never a working key.
WHY THESE ELEVEN ARE ACKNOWLEDGED RATHER THAN FIXED. Repairing them means editing manifests that
deploy to a live cluster -- a Service type, a replica topology, an attestor's verification mode.
Each is a change that deserves to be watched landing, and bundling eleven of them into the change
that introduces their detector would make the detector unreviewable and the repairs unwatched. The
guard's job is to make them impossible to lose; the repairs are the next change, not this one.
KEYED BY IDENTITY, NEVER BY LINE. `key` is `<appId> <valuesObject path>`. A manifest that grows a
line cannot silently re-arm or re-suppress a different defect.
`observed` PINS WHAT WAS ACKNOWLEDGED, byte for byte. If the chart is bumped and the key becomes
half-real, the text changes and the entry stops covering it. A baseline that keeps matching after
the thing it excused has moved is the vacuity class with a filename.
`liftsWhen` NAMES THE GATE THAT WOULD ACTUALLY CLEAR *THIS* ENTRY -- and that phrasing is the
repair of a trap found in this tree on 2026-08-22: a `LIFTS WHEN` STRICTER THAN THE GATE IT NAMES
keeps a deferral alive after its defect is gone. "Lifts when every chart in the tree renders
offline" does not lift when THIS key is fixed, so the entry outlives its own subject and the
ratchet stops ratcheting. Every condition below names one manifest edit and nothing larger.
STALE ENTRIES FAIL. An entry matching nothing is a claim about the tree that stopped being true.
Because each `liftsWhen` above is exactly "this key is fixed", fixing the key makes the entry
stale and the gate goes red until the entry is deleted -- which is the ratchet working, not
failing.

findings.reason: MEASURED 2026-08-22 against argo-rollouts 2.39.5: the chart's key is `dashboard.service.type` (values.yaml:66-68). `dashboard.serviceType` is one word away from real and reaches nothing, so the dashboard Service silently takes the chart default. Not repaired in the change that added this guard: changing a Service type is a live-cluster change and belongs in a change that can watch it land. CARRIED ACROSS A CHART BUMP 2026-09-01: the acknowledgement text pinned the OLD chart version, and the version alone moved. The key was RE-CONFIRMED inert at the new version by the same run that reported the text drift -- an acknowledgement is not carried forward on the assumption that it still holds, only on a reading that says it does.
findings.liftsWhen: LIFTS WHEN this Application sets `dashboard.service.type` instead of `dashboard.serviceType` -- at which point this finding disappears and this entry goes STALE, which is itself refused.
findings.observed: `dashboard.serviceType` is not a key argo-rollouts@2.43.0 has: the chart's own values, its subcharts' values, and every `.Values` reference in its templates name no path at or under it, and no node containing it is consumed wholesale. Helm discards it silently, so the value declared here governs NOTHING: dashboard.serviceType

findings.reason: FALSE POSITIVE OF THE DERIVATION, NOT AN INERT KEY -- acknowledged with the render that disproves it rather than with an assertion. mimir-distributed 6.2.0 ships this key COMMENTED OUT in its values.yaml (`# storageClass: "-"`, beside a note that a per-zone `zoneAwareReplication.zones[*].storageClass` takes precedence). This module derives a chart's schema from its values plus its templates' `.Values` references, and a commented line is in neither -- so the key reads as one the chart does not have. MEASURED 2026-09-01 and RE-MEASURED on the branch that reinstated the bump: rendering 6.2.0 with this Application's own valuesObject emits `storageClassName: longhorn` on the PVCs, so the value takes effect. At 5.5.1 the same render emitted BOTH longhorn and an empty storageClassName, so 6.2.0 is the cleaner of the two. The right long-term fix is for the derivation to read commented defaults, or for the chart to uncomment them; until then this is carried as a known blind spot WITH its counter-evidence.

findings.liftsWhen: LIFTS WHEN mimir-distributed uncomments `compactor.persistentVolume.storageClass` in its values.yaml, or the schema derivation learns to read commented defaults -- at which point `compactor.persistentVolume.storageClass` resolves and this entry matches nothing and fails as stale.

findings.reason: MEASURED 2026-08-22 against spire 0.24.2, and CONFIRMED BY THE CHART'S OWN README (line 124): "In previous versions, the setting spire-agent.workloadAttestors.k8s.skipKubeletVerification was set to true by default. Starting in 0.23.x, we removed that setting and replaced it with" `workloadAttestors.k8s.verification.type`. The pin is 0.24.2, so this key was removed two minor versions before the pin and the manifest still sets it. This is the highest-consequence entry in this file: it governs whether the agent verifies the kubelet, and it governs nothing.
findings.liftsWhen: LIFTS WHEN this Application stops declaring `spire-agent.workloadAttestors.k8s.skipKubeletVerification` -- the key spire removed in 0.23.x -- and expresses the intent through `spire-agent.workloadAttestors.k8s.verification` (whose `type` defaults to `skip` in 0.24.2) instead.

findings.reason: MEASURED 2026-08-22 against weaviate 17.6.0: the ollama modules accept ONLY `enabled` in this chart version. `templates/_helpers.tpl:50,134` reads `(index .Values "modules" "<module>" "enabled")` and nothing else, and values.yaml:1183,1692 declare the two blocks with `enabled` as their sole key -- unlike the sibling octoai modules, which do carry an `apiKey`. So the endpoint and model this cluster believes it has configured for Ollama are not reaching the pod from here; they would have to come from the container's environment. Four entries rather than one because each is a separate declared value that governs nothing. CARRIED ACROSS A CHART BUMP 2026-09-01: the acknowledgement text pinned the OLD chart version, and the version alone moved. The key was RE-CONFIRMED inert at the new version by the same run that reported the text drift -- an acknowledgement is not carried forward on the assumption that it still holds, only on a reading that says it does.

findings.reason: FALSE POSITIVE OF THE DERIVATION, NOT AN INERT KEY -- same class as the mimir `persistentVolume.storageClass` entries above, acknowledged with the render that disproves it. Added by WP18 (2026-09-22, `liveness-kill-budget.ts` slow-starter fix): `charts/loki/templates/_pod.tpl`'s `loki.rulesSidecar` helper renders `{{- with .Values.sidecar.startupProbe }}{{- if .enabled }}startupProbe: {{- toYaml (omit . "enabled") | nindent 8 }}{{- end }}{{- end }}` -- the whole object minus `enabled` is dumped via `toYaml`, so no individual field name (`failureThreshold`, `httpGet`, `periodSeconds`) ever appears as a literal `.Values.sidecar.startupProbe.X` reference for this derivation's static template scan to find, even though the object IS consumed wholesale once `.enabled` is true. MEASURED by rendering this Application's own valuesObject at loki@18.12.1: the `loki-sc-rules` container in `StatefulSet/loki-backend` gets `startupProbe: {failureThreshold: 30, httpGet: {path: /healthz, port: http-sidecar}, periodSeconds: 10}` verbatim -- and `liveness-kill-budget.ts`'s own audit independently confirms it (`hasStartup: true` for that container, up from `false` before this key was added).
findings.liftsWhen: LIFTS WHEN this derivation learns to treat `{{- with X }}...{{- toYaml (omit . "key") }}` as consuming every field of X except the omitted key(s) -- which would resolve `sidecar.startupProbe.failureThreshold` specifically -- the same class of fix that would also close the mimir commented-default gap above.
